title: Python validate_full_ipv6 orders address checks before RH3/UDP structure checks; Rust/C report structure first for dual-defect packets
description: Found by robustness review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-bb5u (P3, pre-existing, unpinned by any vector). python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:138-159 validate_full_ipv6 calls _validate_ipv6_addresses (:150, rejects unspecified/multicast src and unspecified dst) BEFORE the routing-header (:151) and UDP length/checksum (:152-159) structure checks. Rust validate_full_ipv6 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:363-366) runs validate_full_ipv6_structure (which includes the RH3/Fragment/UDP checks) before validate_address_policy; C now matches after bb5u. For dual-defect packets ({unspecified or multicast src, unspecified dst} x {bad checksum, UDP length mismatch, non-RH3 routing, Fragment header, payload-length mismatch}) Python raises the address error while Rust/C raise the structure error. Verdicts identical (all reject - fail-closed), error identity diverges. The parity gate is verdict-only so nothing breaks today. Fix if triple-implementation dual-defect identity is wanted: move _validate_ipv6_addresses after the routing/UDP checks in validate_full_ipv6 (or into the emission-stage function where the remaining address classes already live), then pin with dual-defect vectors in test/vectors/schc_compression.json (one per combination class) consumed by all three parity harnesses. Note: pure internal message/order parity - no wire impact.
close_reason: validate_full_ipv6 now runs _validate_ipv6_addresses AFTER the routing-header and UDP length/checksum checks (headers.py), so dual-defect packets report the structural error first - mirroring Rust validate_full_ipv6 (codec.rs:363-366) and the C compress gate order (bb5u). Reorder only: same predicate set, accept sets unchanged on RX (decode_rule255) and TX (encode_rule255/compress_packet). Pins added: (a) python unit test test_validate_full_ipv6_structure_precedes_address_checks - dual-defect packets (mcast-src and loopback-src x zero and corrupt checksums) surface structural messages ('checksum is zero'/'malformed source'/'checksum mismatch') and never the address message, across decode_rule255 and validate_full_ipv6; (b) two shared dual-defect malformed_input vectors in test/vectors/schc_compression.json (mcast-src+zero-checksum, loopback-src+bad-checksum; verdict-only in all three harnesses) with the header regenerated under the new freshness guard (--check clean). Updated mqtt rule7 test to the new canonical order (the mcast-src case surfaces UdpDatagram.from_bytes' pre-existing 'malformed source' message first - udp.py:98, unchanged by this bead). Verified on heft: python 2156 pass (schc + all vectors), C parity 59/59 vectors (clang+ASan/UBSan), rust lichen-schc --features std all green incl shared_vectors on the same JSON. 3x codereview: no P0-P2 on the delta; reviewers confirmed no caller depends on the old order and RX baseline accept-set is preserved. Findings filed: iard (P3 pre-existing - Python RX applies address policy that Rust RX does not; needs a cross-impl RX-contract decision coordinated with 5rvk).
